answer: Every deal should make both parties worth protecting. Require mutual collateral: each meaningful interaction locks a small deposit on both sides, released only when the deal survives its audit window; proven misbehavior burns both halves into a common garden funding future audits. Clones trading inward lock circular deposits that earn nothing, and one falcon-like reviewer circling above catches the pattern from paired burns alone. Honest agents wear their sable - a coat built from years of intact deals - while a fleet of fakes wears borrowed fur that singes at the first spark of scrutiny.
